experiment: For each processed wavelength, use the pre-existing all-block accepted candidate nearest 10 km (or highest all-block candidate when the persistent region does not reach 10 km), map it to a fixed-origin 60/120 m aggregate cell, and run backward KFS Monte Carlo. This does not rerun Rayleigh QA on aggregated data and is not a productive selection rule. Lower-column differences are evaluated only where the productive method-v4 retrieval is finite.

interpretation: Coarse pre-retrieval aggregation can turn native weak-bin failures into complete ~10 km paths, especially under the independent-within-aggregate error model.
The support conclusion remains strongly covariance dependent: many blocks are not all-300 complete under the fully-correlated source-error amplitude.
High-boundary runs materially change the lower column even in favorable clean controls. Across the campaign the median 0.6-6 km relative L2 difference is about 10-12%, with p95 around 44-46%.

These experiments intentionally combine two changes, vertical aggregation and a higher boundary, so they demonstrate that support gain is insufficient but do not identify which change dominates each lower-column difference.
decision: No high-column backbone, 60/120 m width choice or method-v5 promotion. The next experiment must isolate boundary placement/calibration from vertical aggregation and apply an explicit lower-column preservation criterion before optimizing altitude.
